lessons.title: What I do: verbs with I, he and she
objectives: Say five common verbs in the present tense
Change the verb for أَنَا، هُوَ، هِيَ
Make short sentences with verb and object
starter: Say 'I live in London' in Arabic.
Say 'she is a teacher' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Bismillah and action words
bullets: Today: I write, I read, I go
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Mime actions (writing, reading) and elicit English verbs. Explain that Arabic verbs change their first letter depending on who does the action. Today we focus on I, he and she.

teach.heading: I do: the letter أ
teach.note: Point out the أ at the start for 'I'. Model with actions. Pupils echo and mime. Error: omitting the hamza. Emphasise that ana + verb starting with أ is common.

teach.heading: He does: the letter ي
teach.note: Replace أ with ي for 'he'. Use pictures of a boy doing each action. Pupils say: هُوَ يَكْتُبُ. Remind them that pronouns are optional but helpful.

teach.heading: She does: the letter ت
teach.note: Replace أ with ت for 'she'. Warning: ت is also used for 'you (boy)', so context matters. Show girl pictures. Practise with a quick-fire pronoun game.

teach.heading: Verb + object
teach.note: Add objects: the object takes -a (fatha) as in uhibbu sentences. Practise reading and translating. Pupils make new sentences with different verbs and objects.

practice: Say 'I do not like fish' in Arabic.
Choose the right verb form for each picture: أَكْتُبُ / يَكْتُبُ / تَكْتُبُ.
Create a sentence using a verb and an object.
independent: Write six sentences with different verbs and pronouns.
Fill in the gaps: ___ الْكِتَابَ (أَقْرَأُ / تَقْرَأُ / يَقْرَأُ)
Draw an object linked to an action (a ball for playing, a book for reading) and write the sentence.
exit: How do you say 'she reads' in Arabic?
Which letter starts the verb for 'I'?
lessons.homework: Write sentences about what you, your father and your mother do each day.
lessons.send: SEND: verb cards with picture and mime, limit to three verbs. EAL: bilingual verb list. Stretch: add objects and adjectives to make longer sentences.

lessons.title: Bridge: what is the time now? My daily routine
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I tell someone what I do at each time of the day?
objectives: To understand how to tell the time on the hour and describe my day with times
successCriteria: All: ask كَمِ السَّاعَةُ الآنَ؟ and say the hour
Most: say a routine verb with a time, e.g. أُصَلِّي الفَجْرَ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ
Some: add half past: وَالنِّصْفُ (wa n-nisf)
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: telling the time on an analogue clock
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: our day is built around the five prayers at their times

hook.text: Muslims check the time five times a day. Why do you think knowing the time matters so much in Islam?
hook.a: Each prayer has its time; Allah says prayer is prescribed at set times (an-Nisa' 4:103).

islamicLink.text: Allah says that prayer has been prescribed for the believers at fixed times (an-Nisa' 4:103). Telling the time helps us pray on time.

starter.q: Bismillah. What does أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ mean? A) I go to school B) I come home

teach.heading: What is the time?
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. For the hour we use the 'eighth' form: الثَّامِنَةُ, not ثَمَانِيَة.

teach.heading: The hours
teach.note: Pupils echo. Notice the sun letters: ath-thaniyah, ar-rabi'ah, as-sadisah.

teach.heading: Half past
teach.note: Show a clock on screen at 7:30. Quarter past (وَالرُّبْعُ) is for the most able.

teach.heading: My day with times
bullets: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ: I wake up at six
أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ
teach.note: After فِي the words take kasrah: فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model:
Start with السَّاعَةُ.
Nine is تِسْعَة, so the hour is التَّاسِعَةُ.
Together: as-sa'atu t-tasi'ah.

independent.q: Core: Write four sentences about your school day, each with a time.
independent.a: For example: أَسْتَيْقِظُ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ. أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ. أَرْجِعُ إِلَى البَيْتِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ. أَنَامُ فِي السَّاعَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ.
independent.model: Teacher writes the first sentence with a clock drawing beside it.

independent.q: Extend: Join your sentences with ثُمَّ (then) and بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ (after that).
independent.a: A joined paragraph using ثُمَّ and بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ

independent.q: Stretch: Add one time with half past.
independent.a: For example: آكُلُ الغَدَاءَ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّانِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ وَالنِّصْفِ.

exit.q: How do you ask the time? A) كَمِ السَّاعَةُ الآنَ؟ B) كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟
Big question: tell me one thing you do and when.
exit.a: For example: أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ.

lessons.homework: Ask the time in Arabic three times at home and write a timetable of your Saturday in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: clock face with the Arabic hours around it. EAL: verb cards with pictures of objects (alarm clock, bowl, bag). Stretch: use وَالرُّبْعُ (quarter past).

lessons.title: Asking questions: مَاذَا، لِمَاذَا، كَيْفَ
lessons.bigQuestion: Which question word helps you learn the most: what, why or how? Why?
objectives: To understand how to ask and answer questions with what, why and how
successCriteria: All: say what مَاذَا، لِمَاذَا، كَيْفَ mean
Most: answer a لِمَاذَا question with لِأَنَّ
Some: write three questions about the dialogue for a partner
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: curiosity and asking to learn

keywords.def: a yes or no question word

hook.text: Which question word helps you learn the most: what, why or how? Why?
hook.a: Often 'why?': it leads to reasons. Arabic answers لِمَاذَا with لِأَنَّ.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'So ask the people of knowledge if you do not know' (an-Nahl 16:43).

teach.heading: Question words
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: Why? Because
teach.note: Pupils give their own reason.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: The best answer to لِمَاذَا ...؟ starts with ...

practice.a: For example: أُسَاعِدُهَا فِي المَطْبَخِ / أُنَظِّفُ غُرْفَتِي
practice.model: Teacher: كَيْفَ asks how. Answer with what you do: أُسَاعِدُهَا فِي المَطْبَخِ (I help her in the kitchen).

independent.q: Question cards on the pupil PDF: write three questions about the dialogue (one each with مَاذَا، لِمَاذَا، كَيْفَ); swap with a partner in a breakout and answer each other's in Arabic.
independent.a: Three well-formed questions and full-sentence answers, the why answer with لِأَنَّ
independent.model: Teacher writes: مَاذَا تَطْبُخُ أُمُّ يُوسُفَ؟ تَطْبُخُ الفَطُورَ.

independent.q: Extend: answer هَلْ تُسَاعِدُ أُمَّكَ؟ with a full sentence.
independent.a: نَعَمْ، أُسَاعِدُهَا ...

independent.q: Stretch: ask a question with كَيْفَ about school.
independent.a: For example: كَيْفَ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ؟

exit.q: كَيْفَ means ...
Back to our ponder: which question word teaches the most?

lessons.homework: Ask your mother or carer two questions in Arabic (teach her the words) and write her answers.
lessons.send: SEND: question frames with the question word given. EAL: question word cards. Stretch: write a five-line interview.

lessons.title: Writing about my day: يَوْمِي
lessons.bigQuestion: If your whole day were written in five sentences, which five moments would you choose?
objectives: To understand how to write a short text about my day in order, with time words and joiners
successCriteria: All: write four sentences about my day
Most: put them in order with ثُمَّ and بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ
Some: include a 'she' verb and an attached pronoun
lessons.crossCurricular: English: chronological writing with time connectives
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: a day built around salah

hook.text: If your whole day were written in five sentences, which five moments would you choose?
hook.a: Pupils' own: often waking for Fajr, school, helping at home, family time and sleep.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers with darkness' (ad-Duha 93:1-2).

teach.heading: My day in order
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Order words
bullets: ثُمَّ / بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ: then / after that
teach.note: Recall from the retelling lesson in Spring 2.

teach.heading: Model text
teach.note: Labelled: order word, action, time, extra detail.

quote.text:
أَوَّلًا أَسْتَيْقِظُ لِصَلَاةِ الفَجْرِ.
ثُمَّ آكُلُ الفَطُورَ مَعَ أُسْرَتِي.
بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ أَدْرُسُ، وَأُمِّي تُسَاعِدُنِي.
أَخِيرًا أَنَامُ بَعْدَ العِشَاءِ.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Put in order: أَنَامُ / أَسْتَيْقِظُ / آكُلُ الفَطُورَ
practice.a: أَسْتَيْقِظُ، ثُمَّ آكُلُ الفَطُورَ، وَأَخِيرًا أَنَامُ
practice.model: Teacher: morning first: أَسْتَيْقِظُ. Then breakfast: ثُمَّ آكُلُ الفَطُورَ. Last, sleep: أَخِيرًا أَنَامُ.

independent.q: Write 'يَوْمِي' in the portal response box or on the pupil PDF: five or six sentences in order with أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ، بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ، أَخِيرًا, one 'she' verb and one attached pronoun. Start: أَوَّلًا ...
independent.a: An ordered text with order words, a 'she' verb (for example تُسَاعِدُنِي) and an attached pronoun
independent.model: Teacher writes sentence 3 and highlights the 'she' verb تُسَاعِدُنِي and the ending ـنِي.

independent.q: Extend: read your text to a partner, who asks one مَتَى question.
independent.a: Correct question and answer

independent.q: Stretch: unit check: write two sentences about your mother using a question word and لِأَنَّ.
independent.a: For example: لِمَاذَا أُحِبُّ أُمِّي؟ لِأَنَّهَا تُسَاعِدُنِي

exit.q: Back to our ponder: which five moments did you choose?

lessons.homework: Read your 'my day' text to your family and add one sentence about how you help at home.
lessons.send: SEND: writing frame with order words and a word bank. EAL: model text with English. Stretch: add a sentence in the past about yesterday.

Kitabi Arabic (CHECK IN KITABI for the matching unit and page)

lessons.title: Bridge: the months; my computer and devices
lessons.bigQuestion: How do Muslims name the months, and how do we name the devices we use?
objectives: To understand how to name the Islamic months and everyday devices in Arabic
successCriteria: All: name رَمَضَان and two other Hijri months
Most: say the twelve Hijri months in order with help
Some: describe my device: عِنْدِي حَاسُوبٌ (I have a computer)
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: the Islamic calendar follows the moon, as Allah set it

hook.text: Why does Ramadan start about 11 days earlier each year in the January to December calendar?
hook.a: Hijri months follow the moon; a moon year is about 354 days, shorter than the sun year.

islamicLink.text: Allah says the number of months with Him is twelve (at-Tawbah 9:36). The Hijri months begin with each new crescent moon.

starter.q: Bismillah. السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ is: A) 3 o'clock B) 8 o'clock
Name three days of the week in Arabic.

teach.heading: Hijri months 1 to 6
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Pupils echo. Ask which month starts the Hijri year (Muharram).

teach.heading: Hijri months 7 to 12
teach.note: We are now in Sha'ban, the month before Ramadan. Eid al-Fitr is on 1 Shawwal; Hajj and Eid al-Adha are in Dhu l-Hijjah.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Sha'ban is the 8th month; Ramadan is the 9th.

teach.heading: My devices
teach.note: Pupils show each device on camera. Sentence: عِنْدِي حَاسُوبٌ (I have a computer).

teach.heading: Using devices well
bullets: I use the computer for studying
teach.note: Link to our online school: we learn on these devices every day.

practice.q: Say: Ramadan is the ninth month.
practice.model:
Start with the month: رَمَضَانُ.
The month: الشَّهْرُ.
Ninth: التَّاسِعُ (like the hour, but for a boy word).

independent.q: Core: Write the twelve Hijri months in order (use the slide for help) and circle the months of Ramadan and the two Eids.
independent.a: مُحَرَّم، صَفَر، رَبِيعٌ الأَوَّلُ، رَبِيعٌ الآخِرُ، جُمَادَى الأُولَى، جُمَادَى الآخِرَةُ، رَجَب، شَعْبَان، رَمَضَان، شَوَّال، ذُو القَعْدَةِ، ذُو الحِجَّةِ; circle رَمَضَان، شَوَّال، ذُو الحِجَّةِ
independent.model: Teacher writes the first three in a column, numbering them.

independent.q: Extend: Write two sentences about your devices: عِنْدِي ... / أَسْتَخْدِمُ ...
independent.a: For example: عِنْدِي حَاسُوبٌ. أَسْتَخْدِمُ الحَاسُوبَ لِلدِّرَاسَةِ.

independent.q: Stretch: Find the Hijri date today on an Islamic calendar and write the month in Arabic.
independent.a: شَعْبَان (in late January 2027)

exit.q: Which month is Ramadan? A) the 7th B) the 9th C) the 12th
Big question: how many months are there with Allah, and what is 'computer' in Arabic?

lessons.homework: Learn the twelve Hijri months in order; say them to someone at home.
lessons.send: SEND: month cards to put in order. EAL: device labels with pictures. Stretch: the international months يَنَايِر (January), فِبْرَايِر (February).

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Reading dialogues: a school event; getting to know each other; the heater
lessons.title: Reading dialogue: a school event
lessons.bigQuestion: How do I find the key information in an Arabic dialogue?
objectives: To understand a short Arabic dialogue about a school event and answer questions on it
successCriteria: All: read the dialogue aloud with a partner
Most: answer four questions: who, what, when, where
Some: explain what بِالتَّوْفِيقِ and مَا شَاءَ اللّٰهُ show about the speakers
lessons.crossCurricular: English: reading a play script (speakers, lines, turn-taking)
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: a Qur'an competition as a way of loving the Book of Allah

hook.text: What makes a school event exciting? Think of one event you would like our online school to hold.
hook.a: For example a Qur'an competition, a reading challenge, a charity day.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'So race to all that is good' (al-Baqarah 2:148). A Qur'an competition is racing in good.

starter.q: Bismillah. Which is the 9th Hijri month? A) رَمَضَان B) شَوَّال

teach.heading: Words we need
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. سَـ at the start of a verb means 'will'.

teach.heading: The dialogue

quote.text: سَلْمَى: مَاذَا عِنْدَنَا يَوْمَ الخَمِيسِ؟ / خَالِدٌ: عِنْدَنَا مُسَابَقَةُ القُرْآنِ فِي المَدْرَسَةِ. / سَلْمَى: هَلْ تُشَارِكُ فِي المُسَابَقَةِ؟ / خَالِدٌ: نَعَمْ، سَأَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ المُلْكِ. / سَلْمَى: مَا شَاءَ اللّٰهُ! بِالتَّوْفِيقِ.
quote.source: Our own dialogue for 'a school event' (Kitabi version: CHECK IN KITABI)

teach.note: Read it twice; then two pupils read the parts. Meaning: What do we have on Thursday? We have a Qur'an competition at school. Are you taking part? Yes, I will read Surat al-Mulk. Masha'Allah! Good luck.

teach.heading: Question words
bullets: هَلْ؟ (hal?) a yes or no question
teach.note: Model: مَتَى المُسَابَقَةُ؟ يَوْمَ الخَمِيسِ.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model:
مَتَى asks when.
Find a day in the dialogue: يَوْمَ الخَمِيسِ.
Answer: al-musabaqah yawma l-khamis.

independent.q: Core: Answer in Arabic (portal response box): 1) مَاذَا عِنْدَهُمْ يَوْمَ الخَمِيسِ؟ 2) مَاذَا سَيَقْرَأُ خَالِدٌ؟
independent.a: 1) مُسَابَقَةُ القُرْآنِ. 2) سُورَةَ المُلْكِ.
independent.model: Teacher answers the first, underlining the line in the dialogue where the answer is.

independent.q: Extend: Read the dialogue with a partner in a breakout room, then swap parts.
independent.a: Fluent reading with correct vowels

independent.q: Stretch: Change the dialogue: a different day and a different surah.
independent.a: For example: يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ ... سَأَقْرَأُ سُورَةَ النَّبَأِ.

exit.q: What does مُسَابَقَة mean? A) competition B) school C) prize
Big question: how did you find the key information in the dialogue?
exit.a: By using the question words (what, when, where) and finding the line that answers them.

lessons.homework: Read the dialogue to someone at home and teach them the meaning of بِالتَّوْفِيقِ.
lessons.send: SEND: dialogue with the speaker names in colour and an English line under each. EAL: key words with pictures. Stretch: add one more line to the dialogue.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Reading dialogues: a school event; getting to know each other; the heater
lessons.title: Reading dialogue: getting to know each other
lessons.bigQuestion: What questions help us get to know someone new?
objectives: To understand a getting-to-know-you dialogue and use its questions myself
successCriteria: All: read the dialogue and answer three questions
Most: ask and answer مِنْ أَيْنَ؟ كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ مَا هِوَايَتُكَ؟
Some: say my age correctly: عُمْرِي إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً
lessons.crossCurricular: PSHE: making new friends and being welcoming
lessons.smsc: Social: welcoming a new pupil with salam and kind questions

hook.text: A new pupil joins our class. What three questions would you ask to get to know them?

islamicLink.text: Allah made us nations and tribes so that we may know one another (al-Hujurat 49:13). The Arabic word تَعَارُف (getting to know each other) comes from the same root as لِتَعَارَفُوا in that ayah.

starter.q: Bismillah. What is مُسَابَقَة? A) competition B) prize
Ask a boy where he is from.

teach.heading: The dialogue

quote.text: أَحْمَدُ: اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ، أَنَا أَحْمَدُ، طَالِبٌ جَدِيدٌ. / يُوسُفُ: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ، أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا! مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ / أَحْمَدُ: أَنَا مِنْ مِصْرَ. كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ / يُوسُفُ: عُمْرِي إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً. مَا هِوَايَتُكَ؟ / أَحْمَدُ: هِوَايَتِي القِرَاءَةُ. / يُوسُفُ: تَشَرَّفْنَا!
quote.source: Our own dialogue for 'getting to know each other' (Kitabi version: CHECK IN KITABI)

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Read twice, then two pupils read. Meaning: I am Ahmad, a new pupil. Welcome! Where are you from? Egypt. How old are you? I am eleven. What is your hobby? Reading. Pleased to meet you!

teach.heading: Three key questions
teach.note: To a girl: أَنْتِ، عُمْرُكِ، هِوَايَتُكِ.

teach.heading: Saying my age
bullets: عُمْرِي عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ: I am ten
عُمْرِي إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً: I am eleven
teach.note: Learn these two as fixed phrases; most Year 6 pupils are 10 or 11.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: Ahmad says هِوَايَتِي القِرَاءَةُ: my hobby is reading.

practice.a: أَحْمَدُ مِنْ مِصْرَ (Ahmad is from Egypt)
practice.model:
Find Ahmad's line with مِنْ: أَنَا مِنْ مِصْرَ.
Change أَنَا to his name.
Answer: Ahmadu min Misr.

independent.q: Core: Answer the three key questions about yourself in Arabic (portal response box).
independent.a: For example: أَنَا مِنْ بِرِيطَانِيَا. عُمْرِي عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ. هِوَايَتِي القِرَاءَةُ.
independent.model: Teacher answers all three about an imaginary pupil, writing each on the whiteboard.

independent.q: Extend: In a breakout pair, act out a getting-to-know-you dialogue using your own answers.
independent.a: Six-line dialogue with greeting, three questions and تَشَرَّفْنَا

independent.q: Stretch: Write the dialogue out with a new pupil who is a girl, changing the endings.
independent.a: For example: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتِ؟ كَمْ عُمْرُكِ؟ مَا هِوَايَتُكِ؟

exit.q: كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ asks: A) your age B) your name C) your hobby
Big question: which questions help us get to know someone new? Write two in Arabic.
exit.a: For example: مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ؟ مَا هِوَايَتُكَ؟

lessons.homework: Interview a family member with the three questions and write their answers in Arabic.
lessons.send: SEND: question cards with answer frames. EAL: English beside each line. Stretch: add مَا اسْمُ مَدْرَسَتِكَ؟ (what is your school's name?).
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 6 Arabic curriculum map (2023-24), Spring 1 week 2
Kitabi: reading dialogue, getting to know each other (CHECK IN KITABI); our own dialogue on the slides until checked
Dialogue and question frame sheet (portal worksheet)

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Reading dialogues: a school event; getting to know each other; the heater
lessons.title: Reading text: the heater; reading check
lessons.bigQuestion: How can I show I have understood an Arabic text?
objectives: To understand a short Arabic text about the heater and show it by answering questions
successCriteria: All: read the text and match five words to their meaning
Most: answer four questions in Arabic
Some: explain the safety rule in the text and why it matters
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: heat, burns and keeping safe near hot things
lessons.smsc: Moral: following safety rules to protect our family

keywords.def: we turn off, we put out

hook.text: Heaters keep us warm in winter. What rules should a family follow to stay safe near a heater?
hook.a: Do not touch it; keep things away; turn it off before sleeping.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ taught us not to leave a fire burning in our homes when we go to sleep (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). Safety at home is part of our deen.

starter.q: Bismillah. كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ asks your: A) age B) hobby

teach.heading: The text

quote.text: الجَوُّ بَارِدٌ فِي الشِّتَاءِ. فِي غُرْفَةِ الجُلُوسِ مِدْفَأَةٌ. تُشْعِلُ أُمِّي المِدْفَأَةَ فِي المَسَاءِ. نَجْلِسُ قُرْبَ المِدْفَأَةِ وَنَقْرَأُ. قَالَ أَبِي: لَا تَلْمِسُوا المِدْفَأَةَ، هِيَ حَارَّةٌ جِدًّا! نُطْفِئُ المِدْفَأَةَ قَبْلَ النَّوْمِ.
quote.source: Our own text for 'the heater' (Kitabi version: CHECK IN KITABI)

teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Read twice. Meaning: The weather is cold in winter. In the living room there is a heater. My mother turns on the heater in the evening. We sit near the heater and read. My father said: do not touch the heater, it is very hot! We turn off the heater before sleeping.

teach.heading: Verbs in the text
teach.note: نَـ at the start means we; تَـ can mean she. لَا + verb gives a 'do not' rule.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: When does the family turn off the heater?
check.why: The text says نُطْفِئُ المِدْفَأَةَ قَبْلَ النَّوْمِ.

teach.heading: Reading check: how to answer
bullets: Find the line in the text
Answer in a short Arabic phrase
teach.note: The reading check covers today's text and the two dialogues. Pupils work alone; 10 minutes.

practice.a: فِي غُرْفَةِ الجُلُوسِ (in the living room)
practice.model:
أَيْنَ asks where.
Find المِدْفَأَة with a place: فِي غُرْفَةِ الجُلُوسِ مِدْفَأَةٌ.
Answer: fi ghurfati l-julus.

practice.q: Why must they not touch it?
practice.a: هِيَ حَارَّةٌ جِدًّا (it is very hot)

independent.q: Core (reading check, portal response box or paper): 1) مَتَى تُشْعِلُ الأُمُّ المِدْفَأَةَ؟ 2) مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ الأُسْرَةُ قُرْبَ المِدْفَأَةِ؟ 3) Match: بَارِد، حَارّ، مُسَابَقَة، هِوَايَة with cold, hot, competition, hobby. 4) In the school event dialogue, which day is the competition?
independent.a: 1) فِي المَسَاءِ 2) تَجْلِسُ وَتَقْرَأُ (they sit and read) 3) بَارِد cold; حَارّ hot; مُسَابَقَة competition; هِوَايَة hobby 4) يَوْمَ الخَمِيسِ
independent.model: Teacher does question 1 aloud: مَتَى asks when; find تُشْعِلُ in the text; the answer is فِي المَسَاءِ.

independent.q: Extend: Write the father's safety rule in Arabic and in English.
independent.a: لَا تَلْمِسُوا المِدْفَأَةَ، هِيَ حَارَّةٌ جِدًّا. Do not touch the heater, it is very hot.

independent.q: Stretch: Write one more safety rule with لَا, e.g. لَا تَتْرُكُوا ... (do not leave ...).
independent.a: For example: لَا تَتْرُكُوا المِدْفَأَةَ مُشْتَعِلَةً فِي اللَّيْلِ.

exit.q: What is المِدْفَأَة? A) the heater B) the window C) the kitchen
Big question: what did you do to show you understood the text?
exit.a: Found the question word, found the line, answered in Arabic.

lessons.homework: Read the heater text to an adult at home and check together that your home heaters are safe.
lessons.send: SEND: text with a picture above each key word and two-choice answers. EAL: English line under each sentence. Stretch: retell the text in the past with أَشْعَلَتْ (she turned on).
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 6 Arabic curriculum map (2023-24), Spring 1 week 3 and the review (row 6 reading check)
Kitabi: reading text, the heater (CHECK IN KITABI); our own text on the slides until checked
Text and reading check sheet (portal worksheet)

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Ali Baba and the forty thieves; occasions
lessons.title: Reading: Ali Baba and the forty thieves (part 1)
lessons.bigQuestion: If you found a cave full of treasure that was not yours, what should you do with it?
objectives: To understand the first part of a story in Arabic and the key words that tell it
successCriteria: All: find five story words in the text
Most: answer four questions on part 1
Some: explain what the secret words do
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty about what is not ours

hook.text: If you found a cave full of treasure that was not yours, what should you do with it?
hook.a: It is not ours: return it to its owners or give it to the authorities.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due' (an-Nisa' 4:58).

teach.heading: Story words
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Our own simplified retelling of the folk tale, written for Year 6 (CHECK IN KITABI for the book's text).

teach.heading: Part 1
teach.note: Teacher reads twice; pupils read lines in turn.

quote.text:
كَانَ عَلِي بَابَا حَطَّابًا فَقِيرًا.
ذَهَبَ إِلَى الغَابَةِ لِيَجْمَعَ الحَطَبَ.
رَأَى أَرْبَعِينَ لِصًّا عِنْدَ مَغَارَةٍ.
قَالَ رَئِيسُ اللُّصُوصِ: اِفْتَحْ يَا سِمْسِمُ!
فَانْفَتَحَ بَابُ المَغَارَةِ، وَدَخَلَ اللُّصُوصُ.

teach.heading: Meaning
bullets: Ali Baba was a poor woodcutter
He saw forty thieves at a cave
Their leader said 'Open, sesame!' and the door opened

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: What was Ali Baba's job? Answer in Arabic.
practice.model: Teacher finds line 1: كَانَ عَلِي بَابَا حَطَّابًا فَقِيرًا. Answer: كَانَ حَطَّابًا (he was a woodcutter).

independent.q: Reading questions on the pupil PDF: five questions (three in Arabic), then find and copy every past-tense verb in part 1.
independent.a: Woodcutter; forest; forty thieves; open sesame; the door opened. Verbs: كَانَ، ذَهَبَ، رَأَى، قَالَ، انْفَتَحَ، دَخَلَ
independent.model: Teacher answers question 1 and copies the first verb كَانَ.

independent.q: Extend: predict what Ali Baba will do next (one Arabic sentence).
independent.a: For example: سَيَدْخُلُ المَغَارَةَ (he will enter the cave)

independent.q: Stretch: why do you think the story uses a secret password?
independent.a: It keeps the treasure hidden; only those who know the words can enter.

exit.q: كَنْز is ...
Back to our ponder: what should you do with treasure that isn't yours?
exit.a: Return it or hand it to the authorities.

lessons.homework: Read part 1 to a family member and explain it in English.
lessons.send: SEND: text with pictures above key words. EAL: glossary strip. Stretch: write the leader's words and what happened.
resources: Slides
Kitabi Arabic (CHECK IN KITABI for the matching unit and page)
Pupil PDF worksheet: Ali Baba part 1 text and questions

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Ali Baba and the forty thieves; occasions
lessons.title: Ali Baba (part 2) and questions
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do greedy people often end up in trouble in stories?
objectives: To understand the end of the story and answer questions about it in Arabic
successCriteria: All: say what happened to the treasure
Most: answer questions with full Arabic sentences
Some: explain the lesson of the story with evidence
lessons.smsc: Moral: honesty and the danger of greed

hook.text: Why do greedy people often end up in trouble in stories?
hook.a: Greed makes people careless and unfair; honesty keeps them safe.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly' (al-Baqarah 2:188).

teach.heading: Part 2
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Our own simplified retelling of the folk tale, written for Year 6 (CHECK IN KITABI for the book's text).

quote.text:
ذَهَبَ قَاسِمٌ، أَخُو عَلِي بَابَا، إِلَى المَغَارَةِ.
كَانَ قَاسِمٌ طَمَّاعًا، فَأَخَذَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الذَّهَبِ.
نَسِيَ الكَلِمَاتِ، فَلَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ!
جَاءَ عَلِي بَابَا وَقَالَ: اِفْتَحْ يَا سِمْسِمُ، فَخَرَجَ قَاسِمٌ.
أَخَذَ عَلِي بَابَا الكَنْزَ إِلَى القَاضِي لِيُرْجِعَهُ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ.

teach.heading: Meaning
bullets: Qasim, the greedy brother, took lots of gold
He forgot the words and was stuck
Ali Baba freed him and took the treasure to the judge

teach.heading: Two brothers
teach.note: Compare.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Where did Ali Baba take the treasure?
check.why: To the judge, to return it to its owners.

practice.q: Why couldn't Qasim get out? Answer in Arabic.
practice.model: Teacher finds the line: نَسِيَ الكَلِمَاتِ، فَلَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ. Answer: لِأَنَّهُ نَسِيَ الكَلِمَاتِ.

independent.q: Questions and lesson on the pupil PDF: five questions on part 2 (three in Arabic), then in the portal response box: 'The lesson of the story is ... because ...' (English or Arabic).
independent.a: Answers from the text; lesson: honesty and avoiding greed, returning what is not ours (4:58)
independent.model: Teacher answers question 1 and starts the lesson sentence: 'The lesson of the story is that greed leads to trouble because ...'

independent.q: Extend: describe Ali Baba with two adjectives in Arabic.
independent.a: أَمِينٌ وَكَرِيمٌ

independent.q: Stretch: change the ending: what else could Ali Baba have done that is fair?
independent.a: For example: told the people of the town and the judge.

exit.q: أَمِين means ...
Back to our ponder: why do greedy people end up in trouble?
exit.a: Greed makes them careless and unfair.

lessons.homework: Tell the whole story to a family member in English, using five Arabic words.
lessons.send: SEND: comparison cards. EAL: glossary. Stretch: write the lesson in Arabic.

Kitabi Arabic (CHECK IN KITABI for the matching unit and page)

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Ali Baba and the forty thieves; occasions
lessons.title: Present-tense verbs in the story
lessons.bigQuestion: Stories are usually told in the past. Why might a storyteller switch to the present?
objectives: To understand how Arabic present-tense verbs are formed and use them to tell the story now
successCriteria: All: find four present-tense verbs
Most: change past verbs into the present (he)
Some: use present verbs with he and she (يَـ / تَـ)
lessons.crossCurricular: English: past and present tense in narrative

hook.text: Stories are usually told in the past. Why might a storyteller switch to the present?
hook.a: To make it feel like it is happening now, exciting and close.

teach.heading: Past to present
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Change to the present: خَرَجَ قَاسِمٌ.
practice.model: Teacher: خَرَجَ → add يَـ at the start, sukun on the خ, dammah at the end: يَخْرُجُ. Sentence: يَخْرُجُ قَاسِمٌ.

independent.q: Retell five lines of the story in the present tense on the pupil PDF, then underline the يَـ or تَـ in each verb.
independent.a: يَذْهَبُ عَلِي بَابَا إِلَى الغَابَةِ. يَرَى أَرْبَعِينَ لِصًّا. يَقُولُ الرَّئِيسُ ... يَدْخُلُ اللُّصُوصُ. يَخْرُجُ قَاسِمٌ.
independent.model: Teacher changes line 1: ذَهَبَ → يَذْهَبُ عَلِي بَابَا إِلَى الغَابَةِ.

independent.q: Extend: write two sentences about a girl in the present (تَـ).
independent.a: For example: تَقْرَأُ مَرْيَمُ القِصَّةَ. تَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَدْرَسَةِ.

independent.q: Stretch: what is the present of رَأَى?
independent.a: يَرَى

exit.q: Present-tense verbs for 'he' begin with ...
Back to our ponder: why switch to the present?
exit.a: To make it feel like it is happening now.

lessons.homework: Write three sentences about what your family does each morning in the present tense.
lessons.send: SEND: verb change cards. EAL: past / present table. Stretch: use he and she correctly in four sentences.
resources: Slides
Kitabi Arabic (CHECK IN KITABI for the matching unit and page)
Pupil PDF worksheet: retell in the present

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Ali Baba and the forty thieves; occasions
lessons.title: Reading dialogue: occasions (Ramadan and the two Eids)
lessons.bigQuestion: Which greeting do you love most at Eid, and why?
objectives: To understand a dialogue about Ramadan and the two Eids and use the greetings for each occasion
successCriteria: All: say the greetings for Ramadan and Eid
Most: answer questions on the dialogue
Some: perform the dialogue and add a line

keywords.def: may Allah accept from us and you

hook.text: Which greeting do you love most at Eid, and why?
hook.a: Pupils' own; many Muslims greet each other with تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Celebrate Allah's greatness for having guided you, that you may be grateful' (al-Baqarah 2:185), the takbir of Eid.

teach.heading: The dialogue
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Two pupils read; swap. Our own dialogue.

quote.text:
سَارَة: كَيْفَ كَانَ رَمَضَانُ؟
زَيْنَب: الحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ، صُمْتُ وَقَرَأْتُ القُرْآنَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
سَارَة: وَمَاذَا فَعَلْتِ يَوْمَ العِيدِ؟
زَيْنَب: صَلَّيْتُ صَلَاةَ العِيدِ، وَزُرْتُ جَدَّتِي.
سَارَة: عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ! تَقَبَّلَ اللهُ مِنَّا وَمِنْكُمْ.

teach.heading: Two Eids
teach.note: Compare.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: Who did Zaynab visit on Eid?

practice.q: What did Zaynab do in Ramadan? Answer in Arabic.
practice.model: Teacher finds the line: صُمْتُ وَقَرَأْتُ القُرْآنَ. Change 'I' to 'she': صَامَتْ وَقَرَأَتِ القُرْآنَ.

independent.q: Dialogue task on the pupil PDF: answer four questions, then write your own four-line Eid dialogue with a partner and perform it (breakout, then two pairs share).
independent.a: Answers from the text; own dialogue with greetings and past verbs
independent.model: Teacher writes line 1 of a new dialogue: أَحْمَد: عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ يَا يُوسُفُ!

independent.q: Extend: add a line about Eid al-Adha.
independent.a: For example: فِي عِيدِ الأَضْحَى أَكَلْنَا مِنَ الأُضْحِيَةِ.

exit.q: مُنَاسَبَة is ...
Back to our ponder: your favourite greeting?

lessons.homework: Write an Eid card in Arabic for a family member with two greetings.
lessons.send: SEND: greeting cards with transliteration. EAL: dialogue with English. Stretch: perform without the script.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Ali Baba and the forty thieves; occasions
lessons.title: Retelling the story in simple sentences
lessons.bigQuestion: What is the most important part of retelling a story so others understand it?
objectives: To understand how to retell a story in order in simple Arabic sentences
successCriteria: All: put six sentences of the story in order
Most: write a five-sentence retelling with linking words
Some: add the story's lesson in Arabic

hook.text: What is the most important part of retelling a story so others understand it?
hook.a: Keep the events in the right order, with linking words.

starter.q: Who was greedy in the story?

teach.heading: Linking words
bullets: ثُمَّ / بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ: then / after that
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Order the story
teach.note: Pupils give the order with numbers.

teach.heading: Model retelling
teach.note: Labelled: first, then, after that, finally, lesson.

model.problem: Retell the story in five sentences
steps: أَوَّلًا، ذَهَبَ عَلِي بَابَا إِلَى الغَابَةِ وَرَأَى اللُّصُوصَ.
ثُمَّ دَخَلَ قَاسِمٌ المَغَارَةَ وَأَخَذَ الذَّهَبَ.
أَخِيرًا، أَخَذَ عَلِي بَابَا الكَنْزَ إِلَى القَاضِي.
model.answer: A linked retelling with a lesson

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Join with ثُمَّ: رَأَى عَلِي بَابَا اللُّصُوصَ. دَخَلَ اللُّصُوصُ المَغَارَةَ.
practice.a: رَأَى عَلِي بَابَا اللُّصُوصَ، ثُمَّ دَخَلَ اللُّصُوصُ المَغَارَةَ.
practice.model: Teacher: keep both sentences, put ثُمَّ in the middle.

independent.q: Write your retelling on the pupil PDF or portal response box: five sentences with أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ، بَعْدَ ذٰلِكَ، أَخِيرًا and the lesson.
independent.a: Five linked sentences in order with a lesson
independent.model: Teacher writes sentence 1 of a slightly different retelling.

independent.q: Extend: read your retelling aloud to the camera.
independent.a: Clear reading

exit.q: قِصَّة is ...
Back to our ponder: what matters most in retelling?
exit.a: The right order with linking words.

lessons.homework: Read your retelling to your family; next lesson is the review and check.

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Ali Baba and the forty thieves; occasions
lessons.title: Review and check: the story, verbs and occasions
lessons.bigQuestion: Which was harder this half term: reading the story, the verbs, or the dialogue? Why?
objectives: To understand how well I can read, write and speak about this half term's texts
successCriteria: All: read a short text and answer two questions
Most: change verbs between past and present
Some: write and say three sentences about an occasion

hook.text: Which was harder this half term: reading the story, the verbs, or the dialogue? Why?

teach.heading: What we learned
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah.

teach.heading: Read and check
teach.note: New text (our own).

quote.text:
فِي يَوْمِ العِيدِ يَلْبَسُ عُمَرُ ثِيَابًا جَدِيدَةً.
يَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ يَقُولُ: عِيدٌ مُبَارَكٌ!
quote.source: Our own text for the Year 6 check

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.q: Change to the past: يَذْهَبُ عُمَرُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ.
practice.model: Teacher: يَذْهَبُ → remove يَـ, past pattern: ذَهَبَ.

independent.q: Check on the pupil PDF: read the text and answer three questions, change four verbs, write three sentences about Eid; then say them to the camera.
independent.a: Answers, verbs and sentences from the unit

independent.q: Extend: write the story lesson in Arabic.
independent.a: الطَّمَعُ سَيِّئٌ وَالأَمَانَةُ جَمِيلَةٌ

exit.q: Which part will you practise?
Back to our ponder: what was hardest?

lessons.homework: Practise the hardest part for five minutes a day.

lessons.title: Reading dialogue: my mother
lessons.bigQuestion: What is one thing your mother or carer does every morning that you might not notice?
objectives: To understand a short dialogue about a mother and read it aloud fluently with the harakat
successCriteria: All: read my part of the dialogue aloud
Most: answer two questions about it in Arabic
Some: explain how the dialogue shows birr al-walidayn

hook.text: What is one thing your mother or carer does every morning that you might not notice?
hook.a: Pupils' own: waking us for Fajr, making breakfast; the dialogue shows the same.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents' (al-Ahqaf 46:15).

starter.q: Give a present-tense verb from the Ali Baba story.

teach.heading: Our dialogue
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Teacher reads; then pupils read in two parts.

quote.text:
أَحْمَدُ: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ أُمُّكَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟
يُوسُفُ: أُمِّي تُوقِظُنَا لِلصَّلَاةِ، ثُمَّ تَطْبُخُ الفَطُورَ.
أَحْمَدُ: هَلْ تُسَاعِدُهَا؟
يُوسُفُ: نَعَمْ، أُسَاعِدُهَا فِي المَطْبَخِ، وَأُحِبُّهَا كَثِيرًا.
أَحْمَدُ: وَأَنَا أَدْعُو لِأُمِّي بَعْدَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ.
quote.source: Our own dialogue (Kitabi 'my mother' dialogue to be checked)

teach.heading: Key words
teach.note: Pupils find each word in the dialogue.

teach.heading: Reading well
bullets: Read the harakat on every word
teach.note: Model fluent reading of the first line.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.q: What does Yusuf's mother do first?

practice.q: Read Yusuf's second line and translate it.
practice.a: Yes, I help her in the kitchen, and I love her a lot.
practice.model: Teacher reads نَعَمْ (yes), أُسَاعِدُهَا (I help her) فِي المَطْبَخِ (in the kitchen), وَأُحِبُّهَا (and I love her) كَثِيرًا (a lot), translating each part.

practice.q: When does Ahmad make du'a for his mother?

independent.q: Reading pairs in breakouts: read the dialogue twice, swapping parts; then answer in Arabic on the pupil PDF: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ أُمُّ يُوسُفَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟ أَيْنَ يُسَاعِدُهَا؟ مَتَى يَدْعُو أَحْمَدُ لِأُمِّهِ؟
independent.a: تُوقِظُهُمْ لِلصَّلَاةِ ثُمَّ تَطْبُخُ الفَطُورَ؛ فِي المَطْبَخِ؛ بَعْدَ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ
independent.model: Teacher answers question 2: أَيْنَ يُسَاعِدُهَا؟ فِي المَطْبَخِ.

independent.q: Extend: add a line for Ahmad about what his mother does.
independent.a: For example: أُمِّي تُعَلِّمُنِي القُرْآنَ

independent.q: Stretch: how does the dialogue show birr al-walidayn?
independent.a: Helping, loving and making du'a for the mother

exit.q: حِوَار means ...
Back to our ponder: what does your mother do each morning?
exit.a: Pupils' own, in Arabic if possible

lessons.homework: Read the dialogue aloud to your family and translate it for them.

lessons.title: Vocabulary from the dialogue: what she does
lessons.bigQuestion: How can you tell in Arabic whether a verb is about a man or a woman, even without a name?
objectives: To understand and use present-tense verbs for 'she' from the dialogue
successCriteria: All: say five 'she' verbs
Most: spot the تَـ at the start of a 'she' verb
Some: change 'he' verbs into 'she' verbs
lessons.smsc: Social: valuing the work of women in the family

hook.text: How can you tell in Arabic whether a verb is about a man or a woman, even without a name?
hook.a: The start of the verb: يَـ for he, تَـ for she.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And their Lord responded to them: Never will I allow to be lost the work of any worker among you, whether male or female' (Al 'Imran 3:195).

starter.q: Read the first line of the dialogue.
starter.a: أَحْمَدُ: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ أُمُّكَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟

teach.heading: She verbs
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Mime each. Spoken practice only; no songs or music.

teach.heading: The rule
bullets: The rest of the verb stays the same
teach.note: Pupils hold up a boy or girl card (letters only) for each verb they hear.

teach.heading: In sentences
bullets: My mother works in a hospital
teach.note: Pupils make one sentence about a female relative.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

check.why: تَـ / تُـ at the start shows 'she'.

practice.model: Teacher: يَطْبُخُ is 'he cooks'. Swap the ي for ت: تَطْبُخُ, 'she cooks'.

independent.q: Verb sort and write on the pupil PDF: sort ten verbs into 'he' and 'she', then write four sentences about women in your family using 'she' verbs. Start: أُمِّي ...
independent.a: Correct sort and four sentences with correct 'she' verbs
independent.model: Teacher writes: جَدَّتِي تَقْرَأُ القُرْآنَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.

independent.q: Extend: write the 'he' form of تُنَظِّفُ.
independent.a: يُنَظِّفُ

independent.q: Stretch: write a sentence with one 'he' and one 'she' verb.
independent.a: For example: أَبِي يَعْمَلُ وَأُمِّي تَطْبُخُ

exit.q: A 'she' verb starts with ...
Back to our ponder: how do you tell he or she from the verb?
exit.a: يَـ for he, تَـ for she

lessons.homework: Write three sentences about what a female relative does, with 'she' verbs.
lessons.send: SEND: verb cards with he and she forms side by side. EAL: verb picture cards. Stretch: add نَحْنُ (we) forms with نَـ.
resources: Slides
Kitabi Arabic (CHECK IN KITABI for the matching unit and page)
Pupil PDF worksheet: he and she verb sort

lessons.title: Pronouns attached to verbs: أُسَاعِدُهَا، أُحِبُّهَا
lessons.bigQuestion: English says 'I help her' in three words. Arabic can say it in one. How might that work?
objectives: To understand how object pronouns attach to the end of verbs in Arabic
successCriteria: All: say أُسَاعِدُهَا and أُحِبُّهَا with their meanings
Most: add ـهُ، ـهَا، ـنِي، ـنَا to verbs
Some: rewrite sentences replacing the noun with an attached pronoun
lessons.smsc: Moral: love and help in the family

hook.text: English says 'I help her' in three words. Arabic can say it in one. How might that work?
hook.a: The pronoun joins the verb: أُسَاعِدُهَا = I help her.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good' (an-Nisa' 4:36).

teach.heading: One word, three meanings
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Break the word up.

teach.heading: From the dialogue
teach.note: Pupils find each in the dialogue from lesson 15.

teach.heading: Replace the noun
teach.note: Watch the noun disappear into the ending.

steps: أُمِّي is a woman: use ـهَا

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: 30 seconds, then share.

practice.model: Teacher: أَبِي is a man, so use ـهُ. أُسَاعِدُ + هُ = أُسَاعِدُهُ.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF: rewrite eight sentences replacing the person with an attached pronoun (for example: أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي → أَزُورُهَا), then write two of your own about your family.
independent.a: Correct endings: ـهُ for males, ـهَا for females, ـنِي and ـنَا where needed; two own sentences
independent.model: Teacher does sentence 1: أَزُورُ جَدَّتِي → أَزُورُهَا.

independent.q: Extend: what does يُحِبُّنَا mean?
independent.a: He loves us

independent.q: Stretch: write 'my mother teaches me': أُمِّي تُعَلِّمُنِي.
independent.a: أُمِّي تُعَلِّمُنِي

exit.q: أُسَاعِدُهَا means ...
Back to our ponder: how does Arabic say 'I help her' in one word?
exit.a: The pronoun attaches to the verb

lessons.homework: Say three sentences at home with أُسَاعِدُهُ، أُسَاعِدُهَا or أُحِبُّهُمْ about your family.
